drafts.accepts: Any named service or self-hosted platform that hosts git repositories, current or historical, such as SourceForge.
Any named integrated development environment that bundles editing, building, and debugging for programming, current or historical.
Any named implementation of ECMAScript or JavaScript, current or historical, that executes JavaScript code.
Any named construct or capability of a programming language, described in a language manual, specification, or research paper.
Any named published library for writing diagnostic log messages from a program, in any programming language.
Any named language that embeds structure or formatting in plain text through markup tags or syntax, with a published specification or documentation.
Any named object-relational mapping library or framework that maps database rows to objects in a programming language.
Any named software that installs, updates, or removes software packages and their dependencies, for any language or operating system.
Any named tool that produces a parser from a grammar specification, in any language, current or historical.
Any named tool that measures where a running program spends time or memory, current or historical.
Any named style or model of computation used to classify programming languages, with a recognised name in the literature.
Any named behaviour-preserving code transformation from Martin Fowler's refactoring catalogue or an equivalent published catalogue.
Any library package published on crates.io, which a judge can look up by name.
Any named quantitative measure of a software artefact or process that has a published definition in the software engineering literature.
Any named published library for holding and updating application state in a front-end framework, current or historical.
Any named program that analyses source or binary code without running it to find bugs, style problems, or vulnerabilities.
Any named tool that builds a website of static HTML files from source content and templates.
Any named library that renders text or HTML by filling a template with data, in any programming language.
Any named program that emulates a text terminal inside a graphical desktop, current or historical.
Any named library or tool for writing and running automated tests in a programming language, current or historical.
